To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have expressed and purified a recombinant protein containing the DNA binding domain HMG box 2 of hUBF.

we have successfully expressed and purified recombinant hHMG box 1, which contains 99 amino acid residues with a hexahisitidine tag added to its C-terminus, and it is a single polypeptide chain with a molecular mass of approximately 12 kDa.
we have cloned and heterologous expressed hUBF HGM box 1 from E. coli, and have characterized the secondary structure of hUBF and its binding to the DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression, secondary structure analysis of hUBF and its binding ability to DNA.
the cloning, expression and characterization of HMG domain of hUBFs.
the expression, purification, characterization of secondary structure and DNA-binding ability of hUBF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the HMG box Ⅰ domain of hUBR is a DNA-binding protein, and it can bind to the GC-rich fragment in the rRNA gene promoter and the four-way DNA junction in a structure-specific and Mg2+-independent manner.
the DNA binding domain (HMG box 1) of hUBF is a monomeric alpha-helical structure and it can bind to DNA in a structure-specific and Mg2+-independent manner.
the recombinantly produced hUBF Hmg box 1 is a monomeric protein with a high helical content, and that it has a structure-specific DNA-binding ability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recombinantly produced hUBF Hmg box 1 is a monomeric protein and it has a high binding activity to four-way DNA and a GC-rich fragment.
hUBF HMB box 1 is a stable monomeric protein with a high alpha-helix content.

we have cloned, expressed and characterized the recombinant HMG box 3 of hUBF, which is a monomeric protein containing 54.3 % alpha-helix and no beta-sheet, and it could bind to a four-way DNA junction in a structure-specific and magnesium-independent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recombinantly expressed hUBF HGM box 1 has a similar secondary structure to its natural counterpart.
the recombinantly expressed protein is a good tool in studying the interaction between hUBF and DNA.
the DNA binding properties of the recombinantly expressed hUBF HMB box 1 are similar to that of its native counterpart.
